title: Resources and resource templates
summary: Resources are context data a server exposes by URI. The host application decides what to attach, and resource templates let it address a whole family of items with a URI pattern.
useIf: You have documents, schemas, files or records that a host or user should be able to browse and attach as context.
avoidIf: The model must decide on its own which data to fetch and when, since nothing attaches a resource unless the host does.

explain.md: A **resource** is addressed by a URI such as `file:///project/src/main.rs` or an `https://` URL. Resources are **application-controlled**: the host might show a picker, let users search, or include items by heuristics. The model does not see a resource unless the host attaches it [[tr1]].

A server declares the `resources` capability with two optional flags: `listChanged` (the list can change) and `subscribe` (individual resources can be watched). Clients call `resources/list` and `resources/read`. Results in 2026-07-28 carry `ttlMs` and `cacheScope`. A `resources/read` MAY also return an `input_required` result when the server needs more input.

A **resource template** uses an RFC 6570 URI template, for example `file:///{path}`, listed with `resources/templates/list`. Arguments can be auto-completed through `completion/complete`, which returns at most 100 items [[tr9]]. A missing resource returns `-32602` in 2026-07-28, where earlier revisions used `-32002` [[r1]].

explain.title: Browse, read and watch (2026-07-28)
explain.alt: The client lists templates, reads a resource, then opens a subscriptions listen stream with resourceSubscriptions and receives updated notifications, then re-reads.
explain.src:
sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Client
  participant S as Server
  C->>S: resources/templates/list
  S-->>C: uriTemplate, ttlMs
  C->>S: resources/read uri
  S-->>C: contents, cacheScope
  C->>S: subscriptions/listen resourceSubscriptions
  S--)C: notifications/resources/updated
  C->>S: resources/read uri

explain.title: Subscriptions changed
explain.md: In 2025-11-25 a client sent `resources/subscribe` inside a session. In 2026-07-28 that request is gone. Clients open one `subscriptions/listen` stream and name URIs in `resourceSubscriptions`, and updates carry an `io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId` [[tr7]].

explain.title: Per-user lists are allowed, per-connection lists are not
explain.md: Lists MUST NOT vary per connection, but MAY vary by the authorization on the request. Use `cacheScope: private` for results that depend on the caller so shared caches never cross users [[tr6]].

whereToUse: An IDE attaching files, schemas or git history that the user selects
A knowledge base exposed as browsable documents behind a template such as `kb:///{space}/{page}`
Database schemas and API specs that coding agents should read as context
Targets of `resource_link` blocks that tools return instead of large payloads

use: A person or host decides what to attach
The content is addressable by a stable URI
You want change notifications without the model polling
Large content should be fetched only on demand
avoid: The model must discover relevant data itself and the host cannot attach it
The data needs a computed answer rather than a stored document
Every read must trigger a side effect
flips: The model must find the right item: add a search tool that returns resource links
Hosts do not surface resources: expose the same data through a read tool

pitfalls.symptom: The agent never reads the policy documents the team published
pitfalls.cause: They were exposed only as resources and nothing attached them for the model
pitfalls.fix: Have the host attach them, add a search tool, or return resource links from tools. Verify with traces that show reads of those URIs

pitfalls.symptom: One user sees another user's cached document
pitfalls.cause: A user-specific `resources/read` result was cached as `public`
pitfalls.fix: Mark user-dependent results `private` and key caches by authorization context

pitfalls.symptom: Clients get `-32002` on a missing resource and handle it wrongly
pitfalls.cause: The error code changed to `-32602` in 2026-07-28
pitfalls.fix: Handle both codes while dual-era clients exist

scenarios.title: Attaching project files in an IDE
scenarios.situation: An IDE host lets users pick files to give to the assistant. A code server could expose files by path. Repositories are large and users know what they want.
unknowns: Does the host offer a picker for resources?
Should the model also find files on its own?
scenarios.question: How should the server expose files?

options.name: A `file:///{path}` resource template with path completion
options.why: The user or host addresses any file by URI and only attached content enters context.
options.tradeoff: The model cannot discover files unless the host or a search tool helps.

options.name: A `read_file` tool only
options.why: Works in every host and lets the model choose files itself.
options.tradeoff: Pays tool-definition tokens and loses the user-driven picker.

options.name: Put the whole repository into the system prompt
options.why: It burns context on files the task does not need.
options.tradeoff: Reasonable only for a tiny repository.

flips.if: Users expect the agent to explore unprompted
flips.then: Add a search tool that returns `resource_link` blocks.

flips.if: The host does not support resources

scenarios.takeaway: Resources fit user-selected context, tools fit model-driven access.

scenarios.title: Per-user documents behind a shared cache
scenarios.situation: A remote server returns documents the caller may see. A shared caching gateway sits in front of several hosts. Permissions differ per user.
unknowns: How fast must revocation take effect?
Can the gateway key its cache by token?
scenarios.question: How do you set the caching hints on `resources/read`?

options.name: `cacheScope: private` with a short `ttlMs`
options.why: Responses may be reused only within the same authorization context, so no cross-user leak, and a short TTL bounds revocation lag.
options.tradeoff: Lower hit rate than a public cache.

options.name: `ttlMs: 0` everywhere
options.tradeoff: Every read reaches the origin and cost and latency rise.

options.name: `cacheScope: public` with a long TTL
options.why: Any user could receive another user's cached content.
options.tradeoff: Right only for content identical for everyone, such as shared templates.

flips.if: The documents are public and identical for all callers

flips.then: Keep TTL at 0 and rely on live authorization checks.

scenarios.takeaway: Match cache scope to who may see the bytes.

quiz.q: What does it mean that resources are application-controlled?
options: The model calls them with arguments
The host decides what to attach as context
The server decides when to push them to users
They are always loaded at connection start
quiz.explain: The host app, often through a picker or heuristics, chooses what enters context. The model-called pattern describes tools, servers do not push context into prompts, and nothing loads at start by default.

quiz.q: Put the steps in order for browsing a templated resource and watching it in 2026-07-28.
quiz.explain: The client discovers templates, optionally completes a variable, reads the resource and then opens a listen stream naming the URI to be told when it changes.

flashcards.front: Why can a published resource go unused by an agent?
flashcards.back: Resources are application-controlled. Unless the host attaches them or a tool links to them, the model never sees them.

flashcards.front: How are resource subscriptions done in 2026-07-28?
flashcards.back: Through `subscriptions/listen` with `resourceSubscriptions`. The old `resources/subscribe` request was removed.
An RFC 6570 URI template such as `file:///{path}`, listed via `resources/templates/list`, with optional argument completion (up to 100 items).
